scene.headline: We learned Greek harmony in
metadata: ROME · THE OSTROGOTHIC KINGDOM OF ITALY
BOETHIUS · DE INSTITUTIONE MUSICA · FIVE BOOKS

connections.why: Boethius's Book One retells, after Nicomachus, the story of Pythagoras and the smithy's hammers of 12, 9, 8 and 6 that frame tells, and so passed it to the Latin Middle Ages.
Boethius was born about the time Odoacer deposed the last western emperor in 476, and served Theodoric, the Ostrogothic king who ruled Italy after him.

Cassiodorus, who founded the monastery of Vivarium that frame describes, drafted Theodoric's letters to Boethius and digested his handbooks; the music book reached the Middle Ages in some 140 copies made by hand.

Boethius's Arithmetic, the companion to his music book, is a loose Latin version of Nicomachus's Introduction to Arithmetic, the source that frame follows for the sieve, which Boethius calls the cribrum.
Boethius gave the Greek note signs that the Seikilos stone uses.
